name: crewforge
description: Create, deploy, ask, and test Kubemoot agent crews on Kubernetes from VS Code, through your kubeconfig

crewforge.kubeconfig.markdownDescription: Path to a kubeconfig file. Empty uses `KUBECONFIG`, then `~/.kube/config`.

crewforge.context.description: Kubernetes context to use. Empty uses the kubeconfig's current context.

crewforge.operatorNamespace.markdownDescription: Namespace of the Kubemoot operator, whose report service `kubemoot-operator-report` serves a crew's memory export to the memory view.

crewforge.namespaces.markdownDescription: Show crews only in these namespaces. Empty uses the namespace of the kubeconfig's current context, and shows every namespace you can read when the context sets none or holds no crews. Add `*` to show every namespace you can read (`*` among other entries still means all); a long list is slow through a tunnel.

crewforge.streamTimeoutSeconds.description: Longest a single turn may stream before CrewForge gives up on it.

crewforge.tokenServiceAccount.markdownDescription: `NAMESPACE/NAME` of a ServiceAccount to mint a ten-minute token for when you ask a crew, for a kubeconfig that signs in with a client certificate and so has no bearer token of its own (Talos, kind, k3s). You need `create` on `serviceaccounts/token` for it; the crew then sees that ServiceAccount as the caller. Empty sends the kubeconfig's own token. Only a crew that sets `spec.discussion.access` uses it.

crewforge.tokenAudiences.markdownDescription: Audiences the minted token is bound to, for a crew that lists `tokenAudiences` in `spec.discussion.access`. Used only with `crewforge.tokenServiceAccount`.

enumDescriptions: KYAML, the strict YAML subset `kubectl get -o kyaml` prints: every string quoted, maps in `{ }` and lists in `[ ]`. Still valid YAML.
crewforge.yamlFormat.markdownDescription: How **Show Live YAML**, **Show Source YAML**, and **Compare with Live** write objects. `kyaml` writes KYAML, the strict YAML subset `kubectl get -o kyaml` prints, where no value can be read as the wrong type.

crewforge.dashboardUrl.markdownDescription:
URL of the Kubemoot dashboard for this cluster, opened in your browser from:

- **Powered by Kubemoot** in a chat
- **Open in the Moot** under a crew's answer (shown only when this is set)
- **Open in Kubemoot dashboard** and **Open XLSX** on the fitness dashboard

CrewForge itself never reads the dashboard; it reads the cluster through the Kubernetes API. With a `kubectl port-forward` to the dashboard service, use its local address, for example `http://localhost:8080/dashboard`.
